speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These amendments aim to enhance our audit regulatory regime and introduce measures for better compliance with professional requirements and standards for both Public Accountants (PAs) and Accounting Entities (AEs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These amendments will also align Singapore's regulatory practices with those in other jurisdictions with established audit regulatory regimes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) sought views from the public on the draft Bill last year and have taken in the feedback where relevant and feasible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The first key set of amendments is Quality Control (QC) Inspections.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Today, ACRA is empowered under the Accountants Act to review individual PAs' audit work for selected clients.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: I will refer to these as engagement inspections.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For these engagement inspections, ACRA evaluates whether a PA has complied with the prescribed requirements when auditing financial statements during the audit process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Public Accountants Oversight Committee (PAOC) adjudicates and decides on remedial actions and sanctions for PAs who fail the engagement inspections.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For AEs, ACRA has been conducting QC inspections on AEs that audit public interest entities such as listed companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These QC inspections check if the AEs have the internal processes and procedures relating to leadership responsibilities for quality, independence, ethics, client acceptance, human resources, performance and monitoring.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, the QC inspections are currently not formalised under the Accountants Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This means that when the QC lapses are found, ACRA is unable to mandate remediation or take actions against the AEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will bring Singapore's regulatory regime in line with the practices of other audit regulators in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: QC inspections are useful because they check for adequate internal processes and procedures within the AEs, which should be applied consistently across all engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This ensures that AEs deliver consistently high-quality audit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: If an issue is identified, AEs can make across-the-board improvements that would benefit all engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Mandated QC inspections will complement the existing engagement inspections and make for a better regulatory regime for audit work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This amendment is provided for in clause 12 of the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The second key set of amendments is Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Inspections.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: I move on to this second key set of amendments, which aim to bring our regulatory regime into closer alignment with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FATF is an inter-governmental organisation that sets international standards to prevent global money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As a member of FATF, Singapore is required to meet the international standards set out by the task force.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: FATF requires PAs and AEs to be subject to effective systems for monitoring their compliance with requirements on the AML/CFT requirements; as well as effective sanctions for failure to comply with these requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For avoidance of doubt, let me clarify that AML/CFT inspections only apply to PAs and AEs that carry out FATF-designated activities, which are assessed to have higher money laundering and terrorism financing risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Such designated activities include, among others, buying and selling of real estate; managing of client money, securities or other assets; organisation of contributions for the creation or management of companies; and buying and selling of business entities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: AML/CFT inspections will not apply to PAs and AEs that perform solely audit services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This amendment is provided for in clause 12 of the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The third set of amendments seek to refine the assessment framework for ACRA's engagement inspections for individual PAs and extend this assessment framework to QC inspections for AEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The current assessment framework for engagement inspections is binary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: If a PA fails the engagement inspection, ACRA may impose remedial actions and/or sanctions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, the current framework does not cater for situations where a PA's work may not fail outright, but at the same time, some aspects of his/her work may not be up to mark and needs improvement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Over the years, ACRA has received feedback that such a binary pass-fail system is too blunt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: A more granular indication of how well the PA or AE has complied with the requirements would provide more incentive for PAs and AEs to strive for a better assessment outcome.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The revised categories are: (a) satisfactory; (b) satisfactory but with findings; (c) partially satisfactory; and (d) not satisfactory.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The "satisfactory" outcome, whether with or without findings, gives due recognition to PAs and AEs who achieve good inspection results.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This category will not be subject to sanctions or remedial actions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For the "partially satisfactory" and "not satisfactory" outcomes, ACRA will impose specific remedial actions and/or sanctions on the PAs and AEs for the findings identified.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The findings will indicate the areas of improvement that PAs and AEs should work on in preparation for their next assessment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This amendment is provided for in clauses 11 and 12 of the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Currently, PAs are not required to share the engagement inspection findings on their audit engagement with the entities that they audit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: There is public interest in maintaining trust in audited financial statements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: If there are significant inspection findings on a PA's audit engagement, the audited entity should be informed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will allow the audited entity to work with the PA to remediate findings, which may have implications for its audit and financial statements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It will also act as a powerful incentive to the PAs to remedy and improve their performance, and to the AEs to ensure high standards and internal quality control of the PAs they employ.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: ACRA will also ramp up its efforts to help audited entities interpret the inspection findings on PAs' audit engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: If the PAs disclose the inspection findings on their audit engagements and the audited entities do not know what to do with the findings, we will not be able to raise audit quality.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In short, this set of amendments aims to increase the transparency of inspection findings which will, in turn, promote trust and confidence in the audited financial statements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The amendments also enhance the ability of audited entities to evaluate the quality and effectiveness of their PAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Clause 11 of the Bill provide for this amendment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Clause 23 of the Bill provides for consequential amendments to the Banking Act 1970 to align the terminologies used in both Acts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This in turn will strengthen Singapore's pro-business and trusted regulatory environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: But beyond laws and regulations, I also call upon all PAs and AEs – who have the responsibility to the public to uncover questionable accounting practices and to bring to light potential deception or fraud – to uphold the highest professional standards and safeguard the integrity and independence of the audit process.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help elevate the level of audit quality in Singapore and enhance Singapore's standing as a trusted business hub through better assurance of information available to investors and the public.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This Bill will undoubtedly impact public accountants; they are expected to implement robust policies and procedures under the new quality control standards and sanction orders will also be imposed for non-compliance.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These new quality control standards are a substantial development and change for the audit profession globally, as they include significant shifts in how firms manage quality.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Firms would have to adjust their internal processes and systems to help firms effectively and efficiently implement the new standards.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Based on my understanding, the Big Four audit firms have been preparing to implement the new Singapore Standards on Quality Management way before the standards become effective.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The support could come in the form of funding to help public accounting entities train their staff and/or employ consultants to help with the implementation of the new quality management standards.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One of the criteria is the Shortage Occupation List, which considers talents in short supply on the local job market.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Each job opening that corresponds to the Shortage Occupation List scores 20 points, which will count towards the total score that will determine eligibility for work pass.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many SMPs face challenges in attracting and retaining local talent and foreign talent are needed to fill the gap in the local workforce.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that occupations are considered for inclusion on the Shortage Occupation List based on their relevance to Singapore's economic priorities, the degree and nature of labour shortage and the sector's progress in developing the local pipeline in the medium term to address these shortages.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On that note, I believe public accountants and public accounting entities are of key relevance to Singapore's economic priorities.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They play an important role in the growth and development of the Singapore economy as they act as an industry multiplier, providing professional services to businesses.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Next, there is an increasing power given to the oversight committee and it becomes critical on how the oversight committee members are being selected and appointed.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given that the reviewer has an important role in performing the heavy lifting of the inspection, there should be minimal qualifying criteria for the selection of the reviewers.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on the abovementioned points?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: According to the Global Financial Services Index, Singapore has overtaken Hong Kong to become Asia's top financial centre and the third in the world after moving up three places recently.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This creates many opportunities for the accounting firms, provided they have enough staff to support their growth.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope the challenges of the public accountants and accounting firms are recognised and the Government can consider providing more support as the profession continues to uphold quality in financial reporting and audit as well as contribute to Singapore's position as a global financial centre and business hub.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I support the Bill as it enhances the audit framework.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It also introduces measures for better compliance with professional requirements and standards for both public accountants (PAs) and accounting entities (AEs).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding, I seek some clarifications on the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I agree with the risk-based approach to focus quality control inspections on AEs with higher risk and public interest clients.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would provide a balance between increased regulatory costs and meeting the objective of the said Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, the burden on these higher-risk AEs in terms of financial costs and time would still be increased.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These AEs will need to dedicate time and manpower towards compliance and prepare for the audits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, would there be any form of compensation for the opportunity cost lost by these firms in preparing for the inspections?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: PAs and AEs would have to keep up with the new regulatory regimes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The best way to do so would be through professional upskilling.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would the Ministry provide avenues for PAs and AEs to receive training so that they may meet the new requirements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Going upstream, are MOF and ACRA working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) and our Institutes of Higher Learning to ensure that the new compliance regimes are incorporated into the curricula of accounting diploma and degree programmes?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Thirdly, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we have to stay abreast with the trend of companies moving into the realm of cryptocurrency and even Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) in recent years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is important that we do a meticulous audit of such companies or companies that may have invested in these new monetary realms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is important to note that cryptocurrencies have been used to launder money.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As cryptocurrencies and NFTs are emerging technologies and complex, they may be poorly understood.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would present challenges in navigating through the accounts to ensure that all relevant transactions are properly accounted for.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Building on my earlier point, can we leverage on training programmes supported by the Government to inculcate the necessary skills in our accounting and auditing professionals?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To ensure audit firms deliver consistently high audit quality, I agree with having stringent deterrent measures and penalties.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Be that as it may, this should not be at the expense of impacting the long-term attractiveness of the profession.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Having a clear remediation framework would reduce uncertainty and anxiety, especially for those who are just entering the profession and veterans who are wary about the new regulations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is especially so with the launch of the Jobs Transformation Roadmap for In-house Finance and Accounting Functions and Accounting Practices at the beginning of this year.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The constant call for innovation and transformation is highly relevant as accounting is a profession with roles that may soon be automated.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened that ACRA, as a regulator, continues to maintain a close watch on emerging developments and risks and stands ready to intervene or make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The financial landscape for existing regulated activities has changed and continues to change rapidly, requiring a constant relook at the rules.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Take, for example, some of the key emerging technologies that are disrupting the sector, namely, AI and analytics, intelligent automation, blockchain, cybersecurity and cloud computing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many of these could boost auditing quality, allowing the collection and analysis of broader industry datasets which may previously be less accessible.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Conversely, some of these technologies, being less established or in the hands of someone less technologically-inclined, may give rise to problems in audit quality.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My expertise lies in financial engineering and econometrics.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am speaking on this Bill for a few key reasons.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore is an established international financial centre, but competition for this global position is rife.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We always want to project ourselves further, to be a leading global financial centre.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This means that we must stay abreast with global developments and consistently work on areas that can be improved upon.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is in line with the Financial Service Industry Transformation Map 2025 just launched a few weeks ago to guide our ambitions in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The financial services industry is interlinked with every other industry.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What happens in it has systemic implications across the economy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Accounting is more than a mere reflection of financial information.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Its outcomes move market participants and thereby influences our decision-making.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill will ensure that the information received by investors is transparent and is of high quality.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification has to do with the refusal to undergo practice monitoring programme and review by public accountants and accounting entities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These include refusing to allow a practice reviewer to inspect documents or refusing entry to premises.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These actions are clearly made by individuals who act on their own accord, possibly in defiance of their accounting entity's instructions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify what the Oversight Committee or the Courts should consider in determining whether acts of refusal by individuals are attributable to an accounting entity?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification has to do with the practice review of a public accountant set out in sections 37 and 38.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Based on the report of a practice reviewer, the Practice Monitoring Sub-committee provides recommendations and the Oversight Committee makes orders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Neither authority seems to have the remit to conduct further investigations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is there any opportunity for a public accountant to present their side of the story to the Sub-committee or Committee before an order is served?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After all, once an order is served, it could be 30 or more days before the General Division of the High Court responds to the public accountant's appeal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even if successfully appealed, an order may still have serious professional consequences for the public accountant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, it is important to ensure the right decision is made the first time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third clarification has to do with appeals against the orders of the Oversight Committee.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Various sections of the Bill provide a public accountant or accounting entity who is aggrieved by an order of the Oversight Committee to appeal to the General Division of the High Court.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will enable the public accountant or accounting entity in question to consider whether any appeal is necessary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is important, given that the costs involved in pursuing an appeal at the High Court can be significant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, during the public consultation on the Bill, feedback was provided to MOF and ACRA to redact sensitive information in the inspection report presented to the Oversight Committee to ensure that commercially-sensitive firm-level information remains confidential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While MOF and ACRA noted the feedback, the position taken was that the Oversight Committee will require a full and complete set of information to make considered decisions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, MOF and ACRA also acknowledged confidentiality concerns and stated that they intend to appoint only retired public accountants on the Oversight Committee to ensure that sensitive information remains confidential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Maintaining confidentiality over sensitive information may be a consideration against accounting entities seeking recourse to the High Court.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Once an appeal is filed, sensitive documents reviewed by the Oversight Committee may now become part of the public record.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Accounting entities can apply to the Court for sensitive information to be redacted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, for what reasons will MOF and ACARA reject such requests?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members have raised questions around the three themes of: one, compliance in terms of cost and support for capability building; two, the appointment and powers accorded to the Public Accountants Oversight Committee (PAOC); and three, manpower-related matters within the accountancy sector.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how the Government can help the profession, especially the Small- and Medium-sized audit Practices (SMPs) with the training and implementation of the new regulatory regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Yip also raised the issue of cost of compliance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To be clear, the Quality Control (QC) standards that the Accounting Entities (AE) need to comply with are not new.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All AEs would thus have to maintain a system of QC to ensure compliance with professional standards and the relevant regulatory requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As I mentioned, for AEs that audit public interest entities (PIEs) such as listed companies, ACRA has already been conducting QC inspections on them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If AEs have been duly complying with the requirements and putting in place the necessary QC, ACRA's QC inspections should just serve as a check to ensure that the QC and systems put in place by the AEs are indeed adequate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Also, based on the nature and circumstances of the AE and the engagements performed by the AE, some of the requirements set out in our QC standards may not be applicable to certain smaller AEs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, larger AEs with international networks would need to look into policies relating to network resources requirements, but SMPs with no international network would not have to meet such requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There will be a greater focus on inspecting AEs that audit higher risk PIE clients.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: AEs that audit lower-risk non-PIEs will be inspected less frequently.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, AEs that performed well in their previous inspections will be subjected to less frequent inspections compared to AEs with more issues identified during inspections.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Such a risk-tiered approach is meant to keep the compliance burden manageable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government will also help the profession, especially SMPs, with capability building to meet the new regulatory regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ACRA is already working closely with the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (ISCA), which is the national professional accountancy body, on various initiatives to support the profession.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ISCA has organised webinars and workshops on how AEs can implement the QC standards effectively.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, ISCA has provided tips and examples to guide SMPs on the implementation of the QC standards.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Yip also asked if MOF works with MOE and the Institutes of Higher Learning to update the accounting curriculum.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Singapore Accountancy Commission (SAC), works with IHLs to ensure that the curriculum is up to date and aligned with the Skills Framework for Accountancy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This ensures that accountancy graduates are equipped with the right skills based on the prevailing standards.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, as accounting or auditing standards are regularly updated, continuing professional education for accountancy professionals to ensure their relevance is also important.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Yip also asked whether time will be given to PAs and AEs to remediate lapses uncovered during inspections before sanctions are imposed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Further, he asked about the escalation process for non-remediation of lapses found during inspections.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When ACRA imposes a remedial order on the PA and AE on lapses found during its inspections, time will be given to the PA and the AE to complete the remediation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The remedial actions may include completion of training programmes and/or subjecting certain audit engagements to further reviews before finalising the audit reports.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are existing processes and an escalation framework for the PAOC to manage non-compliances with its orders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will now move on to the second set of questions, raised by Mr Don Wee and Mr Louis Ng, relating to the PAOC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Wee asked how the PAOC members are appointed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ACRA, with the Minister for Finance's approval, appoints the PAOC members.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is a rigorous appointment process to ensure that the PAOC comprises experienced professionals from the public service, the business community and the audit profession.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To safeguard the objectivity and independence of the PAOC, majority of the PAOC, including the Chairman, will comprise members who are non-audit practitioners.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The PAOC members will also recuse themselves if there is a conflict of interest.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is to ensure that decisions taken are impartial and can withstand scrutiny.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Wee also asked about the minimal qualifying criteria in the appointment of the entity reviewer by the PAOC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Entity reviewers are similarly subject to a robust appointment process.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will need to possess the necessary professional qualifications and relevant work experience, at the very least, at a managerial level, in audits or in handling quality control aspects in an AE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To ensure that the entity reviewers stay updated on the developments of the professional standards and practices, they will also be required to undergo training and continuing professional education regularly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Ng raised several questions about the powers and processes of PAOC and its subcommittee.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, Mr Ng asked, what would constitute a reasonable excuse for refusing to undergo practice monitoring programme or a review.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This depends on the facts, applying the perspective of a reasonable person in the PAs' or AEs' shoes at the relevant time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One example of a reasonable excuse is where the PA had been certified to be medically unwell.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, Mr Ng asked what the PAOC or the Court would consider in determining whether acts of refusal of individuals are attributable to an AE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our intent is to ensure that all PAs and AEs corporate with the practice and entity reviewers when they are selected for inspection and to allow ACRA to take regulatory actions against the AE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is particularly so if there is evidence to suggest that the PA's refusal was done with the consent or connivance or was attributable to any neglect on the part of the AE as provided for under the proposed section 38(K)(2)(b).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, if the evidence clearly establishes that an AE has told an individual to simply ignore the review, there is no reason not to attribute the PA's refusal to the AE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The PAOC will carefully consider the full facts of each case, in deciding whether to attribute the acts of refusal by an individual practitioner to the AE Third, Mr Ng asked about the powers of and how the Practice Monitoring Subcommittee (PMSC) and the PAOC can conduct further investigations so that they can make a more informed decision.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The PMSC and the PAOC can and do from time to time make inquiries or seek clarifications from the PAs or practice reviewers, if necessary, to help them make an informed decision.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fourth, Mr Ng asked whether the PA can present his or her side of the case before an order is served.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: PAs are given the opportunity to make written representations to the PMSC and the PAOC before any decision is made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, where the PAOC is of the view that the matter requires an oral hearing such as when complex issues are involved, a hearing before the PAOC would be arranged.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fifth, Mr Ng questioned if the PAOC will as a matter of course provide a written decision on the basis for its orders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, as a matter of practice, the PAOC already informs the PAs and AEs in writing on the findings raised.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The PAOC may in certain cases, provide a more detailed written explanation, for example, where the matter is complex, or the issues raised therein require clarification and elaboration.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, as we will need to weigh all the relevant factors such as the nature of information concerned.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will now move on to the last set of questions relating to manpower, training and productivity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Indeed, as Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng highlighted, accountants and auditors play a critical role in growing Singapore as a business hub.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As our economy grows, so too, will demand for accounting services, both in terms of volume and scope – beyond financial reporting and assurance to also cover sustainability reporting, IT audits, business advisory and more.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is therefore critical that our accounting and audit professionals continually upgrade their knowledge and skills, and stay abreast of emerging areas like sustainability and digital assets, as highlighted by Mr Yip.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This ensures that audit professionals upskill their digital competencies and adopt technology and innovation in their audits.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: PAs can look to the professional accountancy bodies for training and workshops on new and emerging topics.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Mr Yip highlighted, we are also encouraging our AEs to innovate and harness automation technology to raise productivity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The SOL is designed for niche and highly skilled occupations required by the economy where EP holders are required because there are not enough Singaporeans who can do the job, even though wages in the sector are high, particularly in frontier industries.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MOM will place occupations on the list judiciously, through a comprehensive review of evidence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the same time, I also encourage firms in the audit industry to do their part to attract local graduates and mid-career professionals to ensure a sustainable pipeline of manpower in the long term.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The changes ensure that our PAs and AEs continuously improve their high standards and are necessary to ensure the continued integrity of our financial system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is key to Singapore maintaining our reputation of being a trusted global business and finance hub.
